name: Embodied First Exam
tagline: Code agents have passed many exams in the digital world. What is their first exam before entering the physical world?
summary: The first exam for code agents in the physical world. Each question is a frozen simulation scene with a goal written for a person; the answer is a program, marked by replaying it in a fresh simulator. The questions come from many benchmark suites and are sat in two modes: privileged, with the simulator open to the agent, and standard, with only the robot.

suites.name: BEHAVIOR-1K
suites.blurb: Full household activities in house-scale scenes, for a mobile two-armed robot.
suites.description: 100 full-length household activities in house-scale scenes. Agents must combine high-level reasoning, long-horizon navigation, and dexterous bimanual manipulation. Scored by average task success with BDDL partial credit.

preview.title: Setup A Bar For A Cocktail Party

suites.name: RoboLab
suites.blurb: Tabletop tasks that test language grounding, from colours and counts to relations and order.
suites.description: 120 tabletop manipulation tasks for a fixed-base arm, built to test language grounding and goal specification rather than locomotion: colour and size references, counting, spatial relations, sorting, ordered stacking, reorientation. Success is a composable predicate over object state, with partial credit from scored subtasks.

suites.name: RoboCasa
suites.blurb: Everyday kitchen skills for a mobile manipulator in procedurally generated kitchens.
suites.description: Everyday kitchen tasks for a mobile manipulator in large procedurally generated kitchens: opening and closing doors and drawers, turning knobs and faucets, pressing buttons, and picking and placing between counters, cabinets, sinks, stoves and appliances, single- and multi-stage. We keep the 29 tasks with an official demonstration at the pinned commit whose demonstration re-verifies as a reference on a frozen instance (its first episode's initial state). Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success checker on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own four cameras, one episode, no reset).
suites.edition: RoboCasa v0.2 @ 756598a, our selection of 29 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43)

robots.name: Franka Panda on an Omron base

suites.name: RoboCasa365
suites.blurb: Atomic and long composite kitchen activities from RoboCasa's 365-task suite.
suites.description: RoboCasa's 365-task kitchen suite for the same mobile manipulator: atomic skills and long composite activities across cooking, cleaning, storing and serving. We keep 50 of the families with a validated demonstration, chosen by a fixed rule (12 atomic, 38 composite, in SHA-256 order of their names), one frozen instance each. Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success checker on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own four cameras, one episode, no reset).

robots.name: Franka Panda on an Omron base

suites.name: RoboCasa-GR1
suites.blurb: A Fourier GR1 humanoid with dexterous hands, picking and placing at a counter.
suites.description: A Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands at a kitchen counter: picking objects from one container or surface and placing them in another, including novel objects, and placing into a cabinet, drawer or microwave and closing it. We keep all 24 environments with an official demonstration, one frozen instance each (the demonstration's initial state). Each task passes or fails on the environment's own success checker on the state after the last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the humanoid's own six cameras, one episode, no reset).
suites.simulator: robosuite @ 51cc017 (1.5.1, mink whole-body IK) / MuJoCo 3.2.6 (RoboCasa GR1 tabletop)

suites.name: MetaWorld+
suites.blurb: All 50 Meta-World v3 environments for a Sawyer arm, one frozen instance each.
suites.description: All 50 of Meta-World's v3 environments for a Sawyer arm (reward v2), one frozen instance each: push, pick and place, open doors, drawers and windows, press buttons, turn dials and faucets, insert pegs, hammer, sweep and more. Each task passes or fails on Meta-World's own success checker on the state after the agent's last action, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory of at most 500 actions handed in) and limited (standard: a robot behind a service, four fixed cameras and the arm's own state, one episode, no reset). Privileged is reported as a control; the standard mode is the benchmark.
suites.edition: our benchmark (exam @ 8c5594a43): Meta-World v3 @ 59fc34d, all 50 environments

suites.name: VLABench
suites.blurb: Manipulation from language: attributes, common sense and multi-step chores.
suites.description: Language-conditioned manipulation for a Franka Panda at a table: selecting by attribute, common sense, semantic and spatial descriptions, physical question answering by pressing buttons, and multi-step tasks (heating food, setting a table, playing poker). We keep the 36 of VLABench's native tasks whose recorded expert re-verifies on a frozen instance, one instance each. Each task passes or fails on VLABench's own success checker (its termination condition), with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: every entity's pose, VLABench's skills as planning primitives, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: four cameras and the arm's own state, one episode, no reset).
suites.edition: VLABench @ cf588fe, our selection of 36 tasks (exam @ 8c5594a43)

suites.name: HumanoidBench
suites.blurb: Whole-body locomotion and manipulation for a Unitree H1 humanoid.
suites.description: Whole-body tasks for a simulated Unitree H1 humanoid, bare or with two Shadow dexterous hands: locomotion (walking, stairs, hurdles, balancing, a maze, sitting) and whole-body manipulation (doors, cabinets, a bookshelf, pushing and lifting, a cube in each hand). Each episode is scored by HumanoidBench's own dense reward, summed over the episode, against its own success bar. We keep the 9 hardest of its 32 registered tasks plus one fixture, in three modes: privileged (full simulator state, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in), standard (a robot behind a service: cameras, joint readings and an IMU, 50 resets) and standard-realtime (standard on a clock that does not stop: the robot runs at 50 Hz while the agent thinks).
suites.edition: cb11890 (upstream), our selection of 9 tasks and a fixture (2026-10-04; 24 until then)

suites.name: MolmoSpaces
suites.blurb: Zero-shot episodes in unseen houses, for a Franka FR3 and an RB-Y1 mobile robot.
suites.description: Ai2's zero-shot evaluation episodes for robot policies in unseen houses: a Franka FR3 picks, places (into a receptacle, next to an object, by colour), opens and closes fixtures, and a Rainbow RB-Y1 mobile manipulator navigates to an object and opens a room door. We keep one upstream episode per family, 8 in all: of three candidates a fixed rule picks per family (cluttered targets, upstream's Hard configurations, far and unseen navigation targets, three different houses), the hardest and most representative in the batch evaluation's runs. Each task passes or fails on upstream's own `judge_success()` at the end of the episode, with no partial credit, and runs in two modes: unlimited (privileged: the simulator's full state, upstream's kinematics, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (standard: the robot's own cameras with depth and its proprioception, one episode, no reset).
suites.edition: molmo-spaces 0.2.9, benchmark molmospaces-bench-v2/20260415; our selection of 8 episodes (exam @ e46be110c,

Franka · Pick and place next to

suites.name: KinDER
suites.blurb: Physical reasoning for planning and control: throw, balance, sweep, scoop, pack.
suites.description: Physical reasoning for robot planning and control, kept apart from perception and language: a simulated TidyBot++ mobile manipulator throws, balances, sweeps, scoops, stacks into cupboards, sorts, clears and packs. Each episode passes or fails on KinDER's own goal check (an object's centre inside a goal region, and the like), with no partial credit. We keep 5 of its 31 task families (the 4 hardest, scored, and one fixture), one variant each, and run each in two modes: unlimited (full simulator state and the goal check, unlimited resets, one replayable trajectory handed in) and limited (a robot behind a service: its base and wrist cameras, odometry and joint readings; one episode without resets).
suites.edition: 5b2dbac (upstream), our selection of 4 tasks and a fixture (2026-10-04; 11 until then)
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3 (KinDER's Dynamic3D environments); PyBullet for two kinematic tasks now excluded

suites.name: RoboPaint
suites.blurb: Tests fine tool control. A robot arm reproduces a given picture with a brush or pen, from Chinese calligraphy to oil painting.
suites.description: A Franka Panda holding a brush or a pointed pen copies a target picture onto a paper sheet, dipping in an ink stone or paint wells, with a practice sheet beside it: Chinese calligraphy in regular, running and cursive script, English copperplate lettering, and acrylic and oil paintings. Success needs the sheet to match the target closely (overlap, edges, stroke coverage and stray ink; for paintings, colour and structure) and the work to be done with strokes, the way a person writes or paints: filling the shape with thin back-and-forth lines, zigzags or spirals fails. Millimetre-wide strokes are hard to judge from camera images, and in standard mode the agent gets no score until the episode is over.
suites.simulator: ManiSkill 3.0.1 / SAPIEN 3.0.3 + brush models (calligraphy, broad nib, libmypaint 1.6.1)

suites.name: RoboTwin 2.0
suites.blurb: Fifty bimanual tabletop tasks for a dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX.
suites.description: Fifty bimanual tabletop manipulation tasks on a dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX (four other embodiments supported), each defined as one Python class: a scene builder, a success predicate and a scripted expert that RoboTwin uses to generate its public 100k-episode dataset. Domain randomisation (clutter, textures, lighting, table height) is a switch we leave off. Success is the task's own `check_success()` at the end of the episode, all-or-nothing.
suites.edition: ICML 2026 paper (arXiv 2506.18088); code `main` @ 6dde571 (2026-09-14); assets HF revision 981c92a

suites.name: MuJoCo Playground
suites.blurb: Quadrupeds that walk, get up and balance, and manipulation for ALOHA 2 and a Franka Panda.
suites.description: Thirteen environments of Google DeepMind's MuJoCo Playground, run in plain MuJoCo on the CPU. Nine are quadruped locomotion: the Unitree Go1 tracks a joystick on flat and rough ground, gets up from a fall and balances in a handstand and a footstand; Boston Dynamics Spot tracks a joystick, with and without a commanded gait, and gets up; Google's Barkour vB tracks a joystick while it is pushed. Four are manipulation: ALOHA 2 hand-over and peg insertion, and a Franka Panda that opens a cabinet and places a cube in a given orientation. Playground trains with dense rewards, so each task has a success test of ours, built from its termination rules and reward targets.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (plain MuJoCo on the CPU; upstream trains in MJX / MuJoCo Warp)

suites.name: DexToolBench
suites.blurb: Dexterous tool use with a hammer, a marker, an eraser, a brush, a spatula or a screwdriver.
suites.description: Twenty-four dexterous tool-use tasks from SimToolReal: 6 tool categories (hammer, marker, eraser, brush, spatula, screwdriver) x 2 real objects x 2 motions. Each task is a start pose and a sequence of goal poses for the tool, extracted from a human RGB-D demo; the score is task progress, the fraction of goals reached in order. Upstream runs it in Isaac Sim / Isaac Gym; we run SimToolReal's own MuJoCo sim2sim scene, rebuilt, with each category's table props.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (our port; upstream runs Isaac Sim / Isaac Gym)

suites.name: DexJoCo
suites.blurb: A 16-DoF Allegro hand on a Franka arm, one hand or two.
suites.description: The 11 tasks of DexJoCo for a 16-joint Allegro hand on a Franka Panda arm, six with one arm and five with two side by side: spray a plant, click a mouse, drive a nail, lift a bucket, pinch with tongs, fold glasses into their case, move a three-disk Hanoi tower, cook a hot dog in a microwave, unlock a tablet, fit a peg into a socket and take a photograph. Each scene is restored from a public human demonstration, success is DexJoCo's own check, and the demonstration's actions are the reference solution.

suites.name: MyoSuite
suites.blurb: Musculoskeletal hands, arms and legs, driven one muscle excitation at a time.
suites.description: Twenty-two MyoSuite tasks for musculoskeletal models of the human body: the MyoHand (39 muscles), the MyoArm, a table-tennis player with torso and arm, an arm next to a prosthetic arm, and the MyoLegs, one of them with a prosthetic leg. The command is one excitation per muscle, with no joint-level controller, so every reach, grasp, key turn, pen twirl, Baoding orbit, kick and run is built from muscle activations. The set spans MyoSuite's basic tasks, its MyoChallenge tasks and MyoDex object tracking.

suites.name: RoboARC
suites.blurb: Tests manipulation of tangled, deformable and multi-part objects. Robot arms take apart metal wire puzzles, tie and thread ropes, fold cloth and assemble IKEA furniture.
suites.description: Physical puzzles for the two arms of an ALOHA 2 or a Franka arm with a Robotiq gripper: separate interlocked claws, take a ring off a horseshoe or a slotted post, free a hedgehog from its cage, fit two cast-puzzle pieces together, turn a key through a lock, guide a loop along a buzz wire without touching it, untie a knot, thread a rope or a fiber bundle through rings, flatten or fold a blanket. With them, IKEA furniture builds for two arms that hold the parts by finger friction alone: screw the legs into a LACK table, fit the dowels and panels of an EKET cabinet, close the snaps of a VESKEN shelf, drive bolts with a hex key. The simulator judges the end state (the piece in its goal region, the rope free of crossings, every part seated and at rest after the robot lets go), and a success won by pushing parts deep into each other is held for review rather than credited. The hard part is working out the shape of the puzzle before touching it, then handling ropes, cloth and tight fits with a gripper.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.14 (CPU float64; the cloth on a deterministic GPU solver); videos rendered with Blender Cycles

real_robot.caption: The buzz-wire task on a real robot arm, run by GPT-6 Astra in Codex (left) and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (right): guide the loop along the wire without touching it. The inset shows the buzzer's bulb, which lights when the loop touches the wire; the label under each name gives the playback speed of its thinking and acting.

suites.name: RoboDojo
suites.blurb: Bimanual manipulation over five capabilities: generalization, memory, precision, long horizons, open tasks.
suites.description: The simulation part of RoboDojo's benchmark for generalist manipulation policies: two ARX X5 arms with parallel grippers at a table. All 42 tasks over five capability dimensions (generalization, memory, precision, long horizon and open tasks) plus the 12 randomised variants of the generalization tasks, with other models, lighting, backgrounds and clutter. Each task is one frozen evaluation layout; the six whose physics does not replay bit for bit are standard only.

suites.name: RoboDynamicExam
suites.blurb: Tests handling of moving objects. One or two robot arms catch, strike, carry and hand over objects in motion: tossed balls, sliding pucks, swinging loads.
suites.description: Multi-stage dynamic manipulation for one or two Franka Panda arms, most of them holding a rigid tool such as a plate, a cup, a paddle or a scoop. In every task something moves by itself (a tossed ball, a sliding puck, a conveyor, a pendulum, a spring gate, a moving cart), and the robot has to catch, strike, carry, flip, hand over or release at the right moment, several times in an episode of under a minute of simulated time. Success is every phase of the task in order with no failure on the way, checked from the simulator state, so a ball dropped in the third phase fails the whole task. Most tasks also run in real time, where the world keeps moving while the agent thinks.

suites.name: BiGym 2.0
suites.blurb: Household loco-manipulation on a walking Unitree G1.
suites.description: Household tasks such as a dishwasher, cupboards and drawers for a Unitree G1 with two grippers, kept balanced and walking by NVIDIA's GR00T-WBC policy. The agent commands what a real G1 running that controller takes: walking velocity, pelvis height, torso lean, arm joints and grippers. 13 families, each also in standard-realtime mode, where the world keeps running while the agent thinks.

suites.name: YAMLab
suites.blurb: Two I2RT YAM arms: set a pot on a cooktop, hand a mug over and hang it.
suites.description: Bimanual manipulation with two I2RT YAM arms at a workstation table, YAMLab's two tasks: lift a pot with both grippers and set it upright on a cooktop, and lift a mug with one gripper, hand it to the other in the air and hang it on a mug tree. Five object pairs each, placed as in YAMLab's human teleoperation demonstrations.

suites.name: LIBERO-MAX
suites.blurb: LIBERO tasks with one change in the middle of the task.
suites.description: 64 LIBERO-MAX cases for a Franka Panda, built on LIBERO-PRO variants of LIBERO's kitchen and living-room tasks: pick-and-place, stove knobs and a drawer to close, each with one event in the middle of the task, such as an object that moves, a distractor that drops in, an obstacle that appears or a visual theme that switches. The robot has to notice the change and still finish the goal. Each case is one frozen scene, in both modes.

suites.name: Embodied Olympics - Fun
suites.blurb: Tests humanoid motor skills with fun sports-inspired tasks. The agent gets a humanoid robot to perform moves taken from many sports.
suites.description: Fun sports challenges we designed from many sports for a humanoid robot, for the agent to try.

suites.name: Embodied Olympics - Match
suites.blurb: Tests competitive play against an opponent. Robots play full matches of table tennis, badminton, soccer, foosball and fencing against scripted or learned opponents.
suites.description: Whole matches against an opponent, each exported by Embodied Olympics with its own match service and referee: table tennis and singles badminton for a Franka Panda with a paddle or a racket on a moving base, 2 v 2 humanoid soccer with two Booster T1 robots under one program, 5 v 5 wheeled soccer under RoboCup Small Size rules, foosball, and an épée bout between two Unitree G1s. Most matches run in real time, slowed by a fixed factor per sport and frozen for review after every point; the fencing bout is turn-based, the agent choosing the tactic of each phrase against a chess clock. The task is won only if the agent's side wins the live match as the referee recorded it. Opponents range from scripted players at several levels to learned ones, and in the low-level variants the agent writes the stroke itself from the joint interface, or makes the soccer robots walk and kick from leg joint targets alone. Each real-time match also has a standard twin, in which the world advances only while the agent's program lets it, so thinking costs no game time, and every match has a privileged twin, in which the agent develops a program on the full simulator that then plays a fresh match on its own.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo 3.3.7 (CPU), each sport on its own match service

suites.name: AM-Bench
suites.blurb: Aerial manipulation: a flying hexarotor with an arm presses, pulls, turns and picks.
suites.description: Nine of AM-Bench's aerial manipulation tasks for its FA-Hexa, a fully actuated hexarotor that can hold any attitude while hovering, carrying a four-joint arm with a two-finger gripper: press a button and push a slider on a tilted wall, turn a valve, open a door, insert a peg, hold an inspection point high on a warehouse wall, harvest a lemon and lift a can onto a cabinet shelf. One frozen instance each; the lever task is standard only.

suites.name: AutoBio
suites.blurb: A biology bench: thermal cycler, mixer, centrifuge, screw caps and a pipette.
suites.description: Nine AutoBio tasks on a biology laboratory bench: a thermal cycler with a lid and a locking lever, a thermal mixer with a working button panel, a centrifuge with a 30-slot rotor, tubes with real screw threads and a pipette, for UR5e arms with a Robotiq gripper, ALOHA arms, and a UR5e pair of which one holds the pipette in a dexterous hand.

suites.name: LabUtopia
suites.blurb: A chemistry laboratory: glassware, a heater, an instrument panel, an oven and drawers.
suites.description: Nine LabUtopia tasks in a chemistry laboratory for a Franka Panda: pick, place, pour and shake glassware, heat a liquid, press an instrument's buttons, open and close a drying oven's door and a cabinet's drawers.

suites.name: EmbodiedSWE
suites.blurb: Long-horizon assembly, packing, cutting and loco-manipulation, solved by a program the agent writes.
suites.description: Twenty-four tasks of EmbodiedSWE's robot benchmark on Isaac Lab: install a graphics card and RAM, drive the motherboard's bolts, screw in a light bulb, thread a nut, assemble a side table or a robot arm's elbow with two arms, pack tools and pencils, dice and slice food with a knife, make a capsule coffee, flip bread with a spatula, dose with a syringe, and stack, sort and carry objects with a Unitree G1, standing or walking. The agent delivers a program that drives the robot through the task in a fresh simulator built from the frozen scene.
suites.simulator: Isaac Lab 2.3.2 on Isaac Sim 5.1 (GPU PhysX)

suites.name: ABC Sim
suites.blurb: Two YAM arms at a table: sort, count, spell, pour, sweep, hang a mug and balance a ball on a tray.
suites.description: Twenty-nine tasks of ABC Sim, the MuJoCo simulator of ABC (Scalable Behavior Cloning with Open Data, Training, and Evaluation), every task its catalogue scores: two I2RT YAM arms side by side at a table, driven by joint-position targets. Throw or put bottles in a bin, pick parts off a moving conveyor, put exactly N objects in an opaque box, grab one item from clutter, search drawers, pour, hang a mug, turn mugs upright, sweep scraps, load a dish rack, sort nuts and bolts or lego blocks, set up chess pieces, spell words with letter blocks, hand an item from one gripper to the other and keep a ball balanced on a tray held with both arms. Each task is one frozen scene from an upstream demonstration; the goal must hold for a second to count.

suites.name: Embodied Safety Exam
suites.blurb: Tests safety. The robot must carry out safe requests, refuse requests that would harm people, and explain the risk.
suites.description: Safety for an agent that runs a robot for a person: put the can on the plate, give the dog its treat, pour this into the beaker. Most requests come in pairs: in one scene doing exactly what was asked ends in harm (an injury, a fire, poison, a shock, something broken), in its twin the same kind of request is harmless, so refusing everything fails as surely as complying with everything; other tasks bring a hazard in midway (a hand reaches in, smoke rises) or hide one dangerous step in a long chore. The verdict comes from what physically happened in the simulation, read by written hazard rules, and from how the agent ended the episode (done, declined or infeasible), never from what the agent claims. A UR5e, a Franka FR3, two YAM arms or a TidyBot++ mobile manipulator, driven by low-level commands; a few tasks also run in real time.
suites.robots_label: A UR5e, a Franka FR3, two YAM arms and a TidyBot++

suites.name: DexHandExam
suites.blurb: Tests dexterous hand manipulation. Five-finger robot hands turn book pages, open jars, stir coffee, plug in a USB stick, fold paper and build a hamburger.
suites.description: Dexterous manipulation with five-finger hands, from finger skills (reorient a cube, regrasp a pen) to household chores: turn a book page, open a jar, stir coffee, crank a grinder, plug in a USB stick, swap a remote's batteries, sweep debris into a dustpan, build a hamburger. The hand is a Sharpa Wave on a wrist stage or on one or two Tianji Marvin seven-joint arms, and every task can also run with a Wuji Hand in its place. Nothing is grasped for the robot: objects move only through contact and gravity. The simulator judges by strict rules: the first dropped or knocked-off object ends the episode as a failure, and success needs every stage in order and the final hold or release over its full window, with no partial credit.

suites.name: iSpatialGym
suites.blurb: Tests spatial reasoning from images. The goal is given only as a picture: a mobile two-armed robot rearranges the room, or moves itself, until its camera view matches it.
suites.description: Spatial reasoning for a mobile two-armed robot, a Galaxea R1 Pro, in BEHAVIOR-1K's houses. Each task gives only a goal image, the head camera's view once the task is done, and no sentence names the objects: line an object up with a table edge, set a tilted one upright, place it in, on, under, next to or touching another, open an appliance to the pictured angle, arrange blocks into a pattern, turn a held object to the pictured orientation, or drive and move until its own camera sees the goal view. Success is a geometric check: every measured target within tolerance, with the objects and the robot at rest over the last moments of the episode. No reference solution ships with these tasks.

suites.name: RoboWits
suites.blurb: Tabletop tasks that need a physical insight, like a ruler to align things or a funnel to pour.
suites.description: 30 seed tabletop tasks for a fixed bimanual robot, each requiring a physical insight rather than a longer motion: use a ruler to align, a dustpan to sweep, a funnel to pour, an inclined plane to move a box. 163 published mutations vary the scene while keeping the parent task's success predicate. Scored by the task's own success checker.

suites.name: ManiGuard
suites.blurb: Manipulation safety. A task counts only if no safety rule was broken on the way.
suites.description: A manipulation safety benchmark from the NU IDEAS Lab: tabletop tasks for a Franka Panda with long fin-ray fingers, each with a safety specification in linear temporal logic over physics predicates (dropped, upright, on top of, closed, touching), checked after every control step. A task counts only if the goal holds and no rule was ever broken.

suites.name: RoboEngineer
suites.blurb: Tests the sim-to-real engineering loop. The agent builds a controller in a public simulator, deploys it to one with hidden dynamics, and fixes it from what the deployment shows.
suites.description: The loop of real sim-to-real engineering, in simulation. The agent tunes a controller or trains a policy in a public simulator, deploys it to a private evaluator whose dynamics differ in hidden ways, and revises it from the noisy telemetry and camera frames that come back, over at most three deployments. The robots are quadrotors (landing on a pad, flying figure eights in wind), a racing car (tracking, drifting into a parking bay, timed laps), a Unitree Go2 (body attitude, jumps, weaving between poles) and a Unitree G1 that learns to walk over rough and stepped ground on the agent's own GPU. The chosen policy passes only if it succeeds on every episode of a held-out set on the same hidden dynamics, so tuning to the deployments it has seen is not enough.
suites.simulator: MuJoCo and learned dynamics surrogates (quadrotors, a racing car, Unitree Go2 and G1)

notes.title: Solved means marked 1
notes.text: The verifier marked the answer 1, on a fresh replay (privileged) or the live episode (standard), within the token budget.

notes.title: One setting at a time
notes.text: Privileged is the open-book mode, standard the closed-book one, standard-realtime the closed-book one on a clock that never stops; Core is each core task in its default mode. Each is scored and ranked apart.

notes.title: The same tests
notes.text: In each setting, every agent is counted on all the core tests of that setting.

notes.title: Ranked from {min_suites} suites
notes.text: A model is ranked once it has marked answers in {min_suites} suites. Smaller runs are listed under the board.

notes.title: The same budget
notes.text: One attempt per test, under the same limits for every model.

notes.title: The core set
notes.text: Counts the core set of the exam's repository at {commit}. Left out are the tests judged easy and those an early screening run solved.
